# Am I Up

> Free AI-powered sports bet tracker. Paste any source (screenshots, X posts, bookmaker text, Telegram tips) and the AI extracts every bet into a structured row. Tracks closing-line value vs Pinnacle, equity curve, yield, ROC, win rate, max drawdown. Public shareable profile per user. Free, no credit card, data exportable as CSV anytime.

Am I Up is a free web app at amiup.io that helps sports bettors track their real edge instead of guessing. The wedge is the paste-and-parse feature: users paste unstructured text (screenshots of bet slips, X posts, group-chat tips, bookmaker copy-paste) and Claude Haiku extracts each bet into a structured record with kickoff date, event, selection, market, decimal odds, stake in units, and settled status. Bets are stored per-user in a Supabase Postgres database with row-level security and daily backups.

Every user gets a public profile at amiup.io/<handle> that shows lifetime P/L, equity curve, KPI grid (yield, ROC, CLV, win rate, max drawdown, median odds), sport / market / odds-range breakdowns, monthly bars, CLV distribution, and the last 30 settled bets. Users with multiple books (for example a personal book and a separate book per competition or sport) can publish each book independently at amiup.io/<handle>/<book-slug>.

Built and maintained by Neil Macdonald, an independent sports betting analyst.

## Core

- [Landing](https://amiup.io/): What Am I Up does, live paste-and-parse demo, sample profile card.
- [Sample public profile](https://amiup.io/sample): Fully-featured example profile so visitors can see every metric before signing up.

## Learn (glossary)

- [Betting Analytics Glossary](https://amiup.io/learn): Hub for the definitions below. Metrics + strategies that matter in sports betting.
- [What is Closing Line Value (CLV)?](https://amiup.io/learn/clv): Definition, formula, worked example. Why CLV is the truest available signal of edge in sports betting.
- [What is Yield in sports betting?](https://amiup.io/learn/yield): Definition, formula, benchmarks, yield vs ROI vs ROC, why yield is gameable in small samples.
- [What is Expected Value (EV)?](https://amiup.io/learn/expected-value): The single number underneath every profitable strategy, worked examples, EV vs CLV, positive-EV betting.
- [What is ROI in Sports Betting?](https://amiup.io/learn/roi): ROI defined without hand-waving, the stake-based vs bankroll-based ambiguity spelled out, worked example.
- [What is Return on Capital (ROC)?](https://amiup.io/learn/roc): The bankroll-based return metric, why serious bettors track it alongside yield, worked example.
- [Kelly Criterion for Sports Betting](https://amiup.io/learn/kelly-criterion): The optimal stake-sizing formula. Full Kelly, half-Kelly, quarter-Kelly, and the 2× Kelly cliff that turns positive-edge betting into a losing strategy.
- [Bankroll Management for Sports Betting](https://amiup.io/learn/bankroll-management): Ring-fencing a bankroll, unit-based staking, flat vs percentage staking, why chasing losses blows up more punters than losing edges.
- [Positive EV Betting](https://amiup.io/learn/positive-ev-betting): The strategy underneath every profitable bettor. How to find +EV bets by comparing soft-book prices against devigged sharp-market references, and why CLV is the truest test of whether the strategy is working.
- [Devigging Odds](https://amiup.io/learn/devigging): Stripping bookmaker margin (vig, juice, overround) out of odds to get a clean no-vig implied probability. Multiplicative and power methods, worked two-way and three-way examples.
- [What is a Parlay in Sports Betting?](https://amiup.io/learn/parlay): The most popular product on every US sportsbook — and the one with the biggest house edge. Combined odds math, same game parlays (SGPs), teasers, round robins, why the compounding vig makes them a losing bet at scale.
- [What is a Moneyline Bet?](https://amiup.io/learn/moneyline): The simplest bet on any sportsbook. American odds explained (+150 vs −140), how to calculate payouts, favorites vs underdogs, break-even math, when to take a moneyline instead of a spread.
- [What is a Point Spread?](https://amiup.io/learn/point-spread): The handicap that levels lopsided games. Covering, pushing, the hook (.5), key numbers 3 and 7 in the NFL, why spreads are almost always priced at −110.
- [What is Over/Under (Totals) Betting?](https://amiup.io/learn/over-under-betting): Bet whether the combined score goes above or below a number. Same concept in every sport — points, goals, runs, games. Team totals, first-half totals, why the line moves.
